stem: What does consumption-based billing measure?

choices.C: One lifetime hardware purchase
choices.D: Only reserved capacity regardless of the service meter

explanations.A: Meters include runtime, capacity, operations, and transfer.
explanations.B: Many services bill by resource use.
explanations.C: That is upfront procurement.
explanations.D: Consumption meters differ; a reservation is a pricing commitment.

stem: A fictional rate is 0.20 per hour for 120 hours. What is the runtime cost?

explanations.A: That accounts for one hour only.
explanations.C: Dividing by the rate is incorrect.
explanations.D: Multiply hours by the unit rate.

stem: Compute hours double while storage stays constant. Which charge doubles under unchanged linear rates?

choices.C: Compute runtime

explanations.A: The storage meter did not change in this scenario.
explanations.B: Unchanged usage does not automatically double.
explanations.C: The changed meter doubles.
explanations.D: Paid cloud services can bill usage.

stem: Buying a physical server upfront is commonly what?

choices.A: Operating expenditure for ongoing service use
choices.C: Consumption-based billing

explanations.A: Upfront hardware ownership is different from ongoing service bills.
explanations.B: The scenario purchases hardware rather than consuming provider compute.
explanations.C: This is not a provider usage meter.
explanations.D: The organization purchases an asset.

stem: Ongoing provider service bills are commonly what?

choices.C: An upfront asset purchase in every case

explanations.A: Customers ordinarily consume rather than buy those hosts.
explanations.B: They pay for ongoing service consumption.
explanations.C: Ongoing service spending is not necessarily an owned asset purchase.
explanations.D: Ongoing bills need not involve a commitment discount.

stem: Why can retained storage cost money without compute activity?

choices.C: All accounts have unlimited free storage
choices.D: Capacity and operations have separate meters

explanations.A: Retained services may continue billing.
explanations.C: Allowances are bounded and offer-specific.
explanations.D: Storage can incur charges independently.

stem: What should accompany a cloud-cost estimate?

choices.A: Only a total with no meter or usage assumptions
choices.C: A claim that transfer never costs
choices.D: A guarantee actual usage cannot differ

explanations.A: An unexplained total cannot be reviewed meaningfully.
explanations.C: Transfer may be relevant.
explanations.D: Real consumption may change.

stem: A VM is shut down in its guest OS but remains allocated. What can happen?

choices.A: Its OS disk is automatically deleted
choices.C: The subscription is cancelled

explanations.A: Guest shutdown does not delete disks.
explanations.B: Stopped allocated VMs retain allocation charges.
explanations.C: VM shutdown does not cancel subscriptions.
explanations.D: Allocation and retained resources can bill.

stem: A deallocated VM retains managed disks. Which cost can remain?

choices.C: Guest OS maintenance charges automatically replacing all disk meters

explanations.A: Disks are separately billed resources.
explanations.C: Deallocation does not change disks into maintenance fees.
explanations.D: Retained resources may cost money.

stem: A normal budget threshold is reached. What does the alert do?

choices.C: Guarantee a maximum invoice

explanations.A: A budget is not universal shutdown automation.
explanations.B: Budgets do not automatically change tiers.
explanations.C: Consumption can continue beyond the threshold.
explanations.D: Budgets do not automatically delete resources.

stem: Which practice makes a multi-service cost estimate incomplete?

choices.A: Ignoring relevant transfer and storage meters
choices.C: Recording the currency

explanations.A: All relevant components need consideration.
explanations.C: Currency is needed for interpretation.
explanations.D: Region is useful estimate context.

stem: How can a team validate its original estimate?

choices.A: Compare only the calculator's total with the resource count
choices.C: Check only resource existence
choices.D: Treat calculator output as the invoice

explanations.A: Resource counts do not validate per-service consumption.
explanations.C: Existence does not measure spend.
explanations.D: A calculator produces estimates.

stem: Runtime doubles at the same hourly rate. What happens to that linear runtime charge?

choices.C: It halves
choices.D: It stays fixed regardless of consumed hours

explanations.A: No free allowance was specified.
explanations.B: Cost follows hours multiplied by rate.
explanations.C: Longer runtime does not halve cost.
explanations.D: This example specifies unchanged linear runtime pricing.

stem: Why is there no single universal price per subscription?

choices.A: Every resource group has one flat all-service rate
choices.B: All services share a fixed minute rate
choices.C: A subscription commitment covers every storage and compute meter equally
choices.D: Services use different meters and configurations

explanations.A: Groups organize resources rather than defining a universal price.
explanations.C: Discount coverage depends on eligibility and terms.
explanations.D: A subscription can contain many charge types.

stem: Which action limits costs after a temporary exercise?

choices.A: Delete owned resources and verify removal
choices.B: Leave resources because the test was temporary
choices.C: Rely on a budget to stop everything

explanations.A: Cleanup avoids unnecessary retained usage.
explanations.C: Alerts are not universal shutdown.
explanations.D: Local deletion does not remove Azure resources.

stem: Which pricing approach generally avoids a long-term usage commitment?

choices.A: A reservation for a stable long-term workload
choices.C: Pay-as-you-go

explanations.A: A reservation involves a commitment rather than avoiding it.
explanations.C: It prioritizes consumption flexibility.
explanations.D: That creates major upfront commitment.

stem: What tradeoff commonly accompanies a reservation discount?

choices.C: A term commitment for eligible usage

explanations.A: Pricing does not grant permissions.
explanations.C: Coverage depends on reservation terms.
explanations.D: Reservations cover eligible charges only.

stem: Which workload is stronger for evaluating a commitment discount?

choices.B: Stable eligible usage through the term
choices.C: A workload whose eligible demand is highly unpredictable

explanations.A: It may not use the commitment.
explanations.B: Consistent use can consume the commitment.
explanations.C: Uncertain demand may leave commitment unused.
explanations.D: A long term may not fit temporary use.

stem: What defines a compute savings plan at a high level?

choices.B: Guaranteed CPU capacity in every region
choices.C: Commitment to eligible hourly compute spend
choices.D: A single fixed discount covering every Azure product

explanations.A: It is not free storage.
explanations.B: It is not a universal capacity guarantee.
explanations.C: Its terms exchange spend commitment for discounted rates.
explanations.D: Savings plans cover eligible compute under their terms.

stem: Why is Spot risky as the sole uninterrupted critical host?

choices.A: Its discount automatically creates a redundant replica
choices.C: It prevents every guest OS restart

explanations.A: Pricing does not add a failover design.
explanations.B: Spot has no such uninterrupted guarantee.
explanations.C: Compute can still restart or be evicted.
explanations.D: Spare capacity can be reclaimed.

stem: Which workload can reasonably evaluate Spot?

choices.A: A sole server that cannot stop
choices.B: Work unable to restart or retain progress
choices.C: Restartable interruption-tolerant batch work

explanations.A: That conflicts with eviction risk.
explanations.C: The job can recover after eviction.
explanations.D: Spot capacity is not guaranteed.

stem: Regional estimates differ. What should be compared?

choices.A: Equivalent SKU, license, usage, and rates
choices.C: Only advertised compute rate while ignoring license differences
choices.D: Only runtime while ignoring SKU and region

explanations.A: Like-for-like inputs support a meaningful comparison.
explanations.C: Licensing must be aligned for a fair comparison.
explanations.D: The rate depends on configuration and placement too.

stem: What must be checked before a reservation is assumed to cover a charge?

choices.C: Whether the resource name contains the word reserved
choices.D: Eligibility, scope, term, and matching usage

explanations.A: An unrelated commitment may not apply.
explanations.B: Not all products or meters qualify.
explanations.C: Names do not determine reservation coverage.
explanations.D: Discount coverage is bounded.

stem: Why assess unpredictable use before committing?

choices.C: Pay-as-you-go never bills

explanations.A: Demand still changes.
explanations.B: Committed spend may exceed actual eligible use.
explanations.C: It bills consumption.
explanations.D: They change pricing rather than logic.

stem: What does a current pricing-calculator result represent?

choices.A: An estimate based on chosen inputs
choices.C: A guaranteed invoice

explanations.A: Actual bills use actual consumption and terms.
explanations.C: Usage and agreements can differ.
explanations.D: Calculating does not purchase.

stem: Temporary festival capacity has uncertain future demand. What preserves flexibility?

choices.C: Commit all peak demand for years blindly
choices.D: Use Spot for an uninterrupted sole frontend

explanations.A: It avoids an unsupported term commitment.
explanations.C: That risks unused commitments.
explanations.D: Eviction conflicts with that requirement.

stem: Which factor can change a price comparison legitimately?

choices.A: Only whether both resources are in one group
choices.C: Only whether both estimates use the same subscription name
choices.D: Only whether both workloads run for the same hours

explanations.A: A common group does not force identical rates.
explanations.B: Configuration and license terms affect rates.
explanations.C: Names do not align pricing inputs.
explanations.D: Equal hours do not ensure equal SKU or license pricing.

stem: A discounted service still wastes capacity. What should the team do?

choices.C: Right-size usage and assess discounts

explanations.A: Discounts do not eliminate waste.
explanations.C: Efficient consumption and discounts complement each other.
explanations.D: Monitoring helps reveal inefficiency.

stem: What should accompany a Spot worker recommendation?

choices.B: A promise that the pricing discount creates automatic failover
choices.C: A tested retry and interruption strategy

explanations.A: Capacity can be reclaimed.
explanations.B: A discount does not create recovery architecture.
explanations.C: Eviction handling is essential.
explanations.D: Temporary state may be lost.

stem: Why avoid using fictional exercise rates as Azure quotes?

choices.C: The script sets Azure rates
choices.D: Real prices depend on current inputs and terms

explanations.A: Services have monetary pricing.
explanations.C: Local calculations do not control provider prices.
explanations.D: Teaching values are not provider quotes.
